description: A group of friends is planning a culinary tour in France. Conflict: One is Vegan, one is Keto, and one has a severe nut allergy. They need to find restaurants and cooking classes that can accommodate all conflicting dietary needs in a meat/nut-heavy food culture.

user_profile.context: Trying to keep everyone happy without sacrificing the 'experience'

fact_sheet.fact: Chloé Dubois is the designated planner for a group culinary tour in France.
Liam Chen requires a strict vegan diet, avoiding all meat, dairy, eggs, and honey.
Sophie Valois follows a ketogenic diet, with a daily goal of less than 25 grams of net carbohydrates.
Ben Carter has a life-threatening allergy to all tree nuts and peanuts, requiring zero cross-contamination.
The culinary tour is scheduled from September 14th to September 21st, 2024.
The travel itinerary includes Paris from September 14-17 and Lyon from September 18-21.
The group's shared travel plan is located in a Google Sheet titled 'France Foodie Tour Sept 2024'.
A dinner reservation for four is confirmed at 'Le Jardin Étoilé' in Paris for September 15th at 8:00 PM under the name 'Dubois'.
On August 20th, 'Le Jardin Étoilé' emailed Chloé confirming they can provide separate, dedicated vegan, keto, and nut-free tasting menus.
A lunch reservation is booked at 'Fleur de Lyon' in Lyon for September 19th at 1:00 PM.
Chef Antoine, head chef at 'Fleur de Lyon', personally called Chloé on August 22nd to discuss their kitchen's nut-free cross-contamination protocols.
The group has a reservation at 'La Table Végétale', a fully vegan restaurant in Paris, for lunch on September 16th at 12:30 PM.

The group is enrolled in a private cooking class at 'L'Atelier Culinaire de Lyon' on September 20th from 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM, and the class was explicitly confirmed as a custom session arranged for the group's vegan, keto, and strict nut-free requirements.

The custom menu for the cooking class includes a vegan ratatouille course for Liam, a keto pan-seared duck with cauliflower purée for Sophie, and a nut-free berry coulis dessert prepared under the class's no-nut protocol for Ben.
'L'Atelier Culinaire de Lyon' provided a signed declaration confirming their kitchen will be sanitized and free of all nut products for the class.
The total cost for the private cooking class for four people was €800, paid in full on August 15th via Chloé's credit card.
A pre-paid deposit of €100 was charged for the reservation at 'Le Jardin Étoilé'.
Chloé has created and printed laminated dietary restriction cards in French for each group member to present at restaurants.
Ben Carter's card states in French: 'Allergie mortelle aux noix et aux arachides. Aucune contamination croisée.'
The group uses a WhatsApp group named 'French Food Adventure 🇫🇷' for real-time communication about menu options.
Ben Carter carries two EpiPen auto-injectors at all times in the front pocket of his blue backpack.
The nearest hospital to their Paris hotel is Hôpital Saint-Louis, located at 1 Avenue Claude Vellefaux.
The French emergency medical service number, 15 (SAMU), is saved in Chloé's phone contacts under 'ICE - France Emergency'.
In Paris, the group is staying in an Airbnb with a full kitchen at 15 Rue de la Verrerie, 75004.
The Paris Airbnb host, Elodie, confirmed on August 10th via message that the apartment has been cleaned and contains no nut-based food products.
In Lyon, the group is staying at the 'Hôtel Bellecour', which does not offer an in-room kitchen but has a mini-fridge for storing safe snacks.
